# Results and metrics (auto-generated by `python -m floodready report`)

All flood scenarios, stock, depot and fleet are GENERATED (seed 42; see `datasets/synthetic/ASSUMPTIONS.md`). Results show how the method
behaves under stated assumptions; they are not measurements of a real flood.

## 1. Data profile (real open data)

- 1,188 villages, 1,622,303 residents, 3,525 km of road in 1,136 segments, 87 human-health facilities (5.4 per 100,000 residents).
- Facility cleaning: 119 'Medical' entries, 32 veterinary removed.
- Before any flood: median 10.1 min to the nearest facility, 90th percentile 24.3 min; 63,853 residents live over 30 min away; 14,405 residents are in villages not connected to any facility in the road data.
- Road network: 2,223 nodes, 2,943 edges; 98.7% of segments in one network at 10 m snapping.
- A facility serves a median 13,895 residents (maximum 108,804); 11 serve nobody on a travel-time basis; 18 serve over 30,000.
- Generated stock: median 14.1 days of cover; 40 of 87 facilities hold under 14 days.

## 2. Validation checks

- Road circuity (road distance / straight line to the nearest facility): median 1.37, 90th percentile 2.64. Plausible (1 to 2): True.
- Nearest facility by road time equals nearest by straight line for 70% of residents (the generated stock used straight-line catchments; a known mismatch).
- Residents assigned to facilities equal connected residents: True. Cut-off share rises with severity: True (mild 3.2%, moderate 22.4%, severe 45.8%).

Capture rate (share of avoidable unmet demand removed by the access-aware optimiser, three hubs): 2 trucks 100%, 4 trucks 100%, 8 trucks 100%.
Remaining unmet demand is unavoidable by road delivery: it sits in villages that are cut off or facilities that no truck can reach.

## 7. Robustness and sensitivity

- Network joining (mean residents cut off): 5 m: 22.8%; 10 m: 22.7%; 25 m: 21.5%.
- Travel speed (+/-20%): mean time after flood x0.8: 17.5 min; x1.0: 14.6 min; x1.2: 12.6 min; residents cut off unchanged.
- Missing roads (random share of real roads absent from our data): 5%: top-10 worst villages overlap 80%, cut-off share shifts +0.4 points; 10%: top-10 worst villages overlap 76%, cut-off share shifts +0.2 points; 20%: top-10 worst villages overlap 57%, cut-off share shifts -0.4 points.
- Depot stock, horizon, trucks and demand rate sweeps are in `sensitivity.csv` and figure R4.
